title: [AUG-107] Sniff audiotee PCM sample format instead of assuming s16le
why_we_need_this:
Follow-up to AUG-105. The coreaudio-tap path in @server/src/services/systemCapture.ts pipes audiotee stdout into ffmpeg as raw PCM and assumes the format from config.audioteeSampleFormat (default s16le, env override AUDIOTEE_SAMPLE_FORMAT). The audiotee README says output is 32-bit float unless a sample-rate conversion happens, in which case it is 16-bit. That rule is undocumented in detail and may differ between builds; a wrong guess produces a WAV of white noise and a garbage [Them] transcript with no error anywhere.

Design:
1. Before starting the real capture (or inside the self-test from the sibling task), spawn `audiotee --sample-rate 16000`, read ~200 ms of stdout (about 6400 bytes at 16 kHz mono s16le), then kill it.
2. Interpret the buffer both ways and score each: as int16 and as float32 little-endian. Real audio has a low zero-crossing rate and a bounded amplitude; a wrong interpretation looks like white noise (zero-crossing rate near 0.5) or contains NaN/inf or values far outside [-1, 1] for float32.
3. Choose the format with the lower zero-crossing rate; if the float32 view contains any non-finite value, pick s16le.
4. Cache the detected format alongside the capability cache and report it in CaptureCapabilities as sampleFormat.
5. Keep AUDIOTEE_SAMPLE_FORMAT as an explicit override that skips detection.
acceptance_criteria:
- On macOS with audiotee on PATH, GET /api/capture/capabilities reports sampleFormat 's16le' or 'f32le' matching the binary's real output, and the resulting audio-system.wav is audible speech, not noise.
- Unit tests feed synthetic s16le and f32le sine-wave buffers to the detector and it identifies both correctly; a silent buffer falls back to s16le without throwing.
- Setting AUDIOTEE_SAMPLE_FORMAT skips detection and is echoed back in the capabilities response.
- Detection adds no more than 500 ms to the first capabilities probe and nothing to cached probes.
- project-context/architecture README replaces the "unverified" note with the detection rule.
important_constraints:
- Do not add sox or any other native dependency; pure Node buffer inspection only.
- The detector must be a pure function over a Buffer so it is unit-testable on Windows.
